PSC DOCKET NO. 17-0977
ORDER NO. 11019
AND NOW, this 20ft day of May 2026, the Delaware Public Service Commission
('oCommission") determines and orders the following:
WHEREAS, on August 17, 2017, Delmarva Power and Light Company (Delmarva" or
the "Company") filed an application ("Docket 17-0977") for an increase in electric distribution
rates; and
WHEREAS' on August 21, 2018, the Delaware Public Service Commission (the
"Commission") adopted Order No. 9248 in Docket No. 17-0977, which approved a settlement
agreement (the "settlement Agreement") entered into by all parties in Docket 17-0977; and
WHEREAS, Section II.1.(c) of the Settlement Agreemdnt addressed the impact of the Tax
Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (TCJA") and the process for how the Company's Excess Deferred
Income Taxes ("EDIT") would be flowed back to customers; specifically, $44.3 million of non-
protected property related EDIT was to be flowed back using a six-year amortization period, and
$20.8 million of non-protected non-property related EDIT was to be flowed back using a five-year
amortization period; I and
t $62.5 million and $29.3 million respectively when grossed up by the revenue conversion factor of 1.40926

PSC Docket No. 17-0977, Order No. 11019 Cont'd
WHEREAS' on March 31,2026, Delmarva filed an application (the "Application") to
modiff its electric Rider "EDIT" Excess Defened Income Tax Credit ("Rider EDIT"); and
WHEREAS, Delmarva intends to reset to zero ($0.000000) certain Rider EDIT service
classifications whose EDIT liability balances have been fully credited to the respective customers;
and
WHEREAS, pursuant to Section II.l.(c)(vii) of the Settlement Agreement, because the
amounts due to the customers in each service classification could not be calculated precisely at the
time of the Settlement Agreement, the parties agreed that any amounts paid to customers in excess
of the total EDIT balance will be recorded as a regulatory asset with a retum at the Company's
Commission authorized rate of return to be recovered in the Company's subsequent rate case; and
WHEREAS, Delmarva has requested similar treatment to that received in PSC Order No.
10135, issued December 14,2022, PSC Order No. 10179, issued February 22,2023, PSC Order
No. 10282, issued August 23,2023,PSC OrderNo. 10338, issuedNovember 29,2023,PSC Order
No. 10518, issued August 21, 2024, and PSC Order No. 10941, issued January 28,2026, that
instead of carrying a regulatory asset balance for the five-year EDIT credits, any regulatory asset
balance be transferred to the respective six-year regulatory liability balance to reduce the
remaining liability if that balance still has a credit; and
WHEREAS, per Schedule 1 of the Application, the General Service - Water Heating
("GS-WH") five-year EDIT balance is estimated to be fully credited to the rate class by end of
May 2026. The Company intends to set the five-year EDIT credit for this rate class to zero
effective June l, 2026; and
2

PSC Docket No. 17-0917, Order No. 11019 Cont'd
WHEREAS, the Company requests authority to transfer any regulatory asset balance for
the GS-WH five-year EDIT credit to the respective six-year EDIT liability balance, thus reducing
the respective six-year EDIT liability balance; and
WHEREAS, Staff submitted a memorandum to the Commission recommending that the
five-year EDIT credit for the GS-WH rate class be set to zero effective June 1, 2026, and that any
regulatory asset balance for this rate class be transferred to the respective six-year EDIT liability
balance;
NOW, THEREFORE,IT IS HEREBY ORDERED BY THE AFFIRMATIVE
VOTE OF NOT F'EWER THAN THREE COMMISSIONERS:
1. 
That the five-year EDIT credit for the GS-WH rate class be set to zero ($0.000000)
effective June 1, 2026.
2. 
That any regulatory asset balance from the five-year EDIT credit for the GS-WH
rate class be transferred to the respective six-year EDIT liability.
3. 
Delmarva is hereby notified that it will be assessed the costs of this proceeding
pursuant to 26 Del. C. $ 114(b).
4. 
The Commission reserves the jurisdiction and authority to enter such further orders
in this matter as may be deemed necessary or proper.
BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION:
Harold Gray, Chairman
